name: Stanley Turrentine
description: '''Stanley William Turrentine''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|t|ɜːr|.|ɪ|n|ˌ|t|iː|n}} {{Respell|TUR|in|TEEN}}; April 5, 1934 – September 12, 2000),'''''' nicknamed '''Mr. T''', was an American [[Grammy Awards|Grammy]]-nominated [[jazz]] [[tenor saxophone|tenor saxophonist]] and record producer. He began his career playing [[R&B]] for [[Earl Bostic]] and, later, recording [[soul jazz]] for the [[Blue Note Records|Blue Note]] label from 1960, touching on [[jazz fusion]] during a stint on [[CTI Records|CTI]] in the 1970s. He was described by the critic Steve Huey as "renowned for his distinctively thick, rippling tone [and] earthy grounding in the blues." In the 1960s, Turrentine was married to organist [[Shirley Scott]], with whom he frequently recorded, and he was the younger brother of trumpeter [[Tommy Turrentine]], with whom he also recorded.
